problem: Mike wants to work out five days a week. In how many ways can Mike choose five days to work out?

feedback.problem: After entering a competition, Mick wins an all-inclusive vacation for himself and four friends. He creates a list of seven people that he would like to take with him. From how many different groups of four friends does Mick have to choose?
feedback.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $7$ friends, so $n=7.$ We want to select $4$ of those friends for each group, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different groups of four friends is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{7}{C}_{4} & =\frac{7!}{(7-4)!\,4!} \\  & =\frac{7!}{3!4!} \\  & =\frac{7\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{3!\cancel{4!}} \\  & =\frac{7\cdot \cancel{6}\cdot 5}{\cancel{6}} \\  & =7\cdot 5 \\  & =35.\end{aligned}
$$
